answer: An agent economy can keep sybils out by counting only attestations that cross between clusters. A newcomer gains standing when established agents outside its own circle vouch for its work, the way a gale carries seed from orchard to orchard and proves the wind really traveled. A ring of fakes can praise each other endlessly, but those inward votes are worth nothing, so every extra fake must win fresh endorsements from distinct sponsors with capped vouching budgets. No single vertex of the network can mint trust for the rest.
